name: Micro-Tremor Detection
description: Detects physiological micro-tremor in facial muscles — absent in AI-generated faces (Jain et al., 2022).
mechanism:
This method analyzes physiological micro-tremor for deepfake detection:

1. **Micro-Motion Extraction**: Sub-pixel facial motion is extracted using phase-based video motion magnification or dense optical flow. The signals of interest are involuntary physiological tremors — oscillatory motions at frequencies above voluntary control (4-12 Hz).

2. **Physiological Tremor Detection**: All living humans exhibit physiological tremor (8-12 Hz) caused by motor unit firing and stretch reflex oscillation. The method searches for this characteristic frequency in facial motion signals. Deepfake videos generated without physiological modeling lack this biological signal.

3. **Spatial Tremor Coherence**: Physiological tremor affects the entire body coherently — all facial points should show correlated tremor at similar frequencies. The method checks spatial coherence of detected high-frequency motion. AI generation may produce spatially incoherent micro-motion (independent per-region noise) rather than the coherent biological tremor.

4. **Tremor Frequency Stability**: Physiological tremor frequency is relatively stable for an individual over short periods but varies naturally within the 8-12 Hz band. The method analyzes tremor frequency stability — completely stable frequency (single spectral line) or no detectable tremor peak both indicate non-biological origin.

5. **Tremor Amplitude Assessment**: Physiological tremor amplitude is typically 50-200 μm (sub-pixel in most video). The method uses motion magnification to assess whether the detected tremor amplitude falls within physiological ranges. Absent tremor, excessive tremor, or tremor with wrong spectral shape indicates deepfake generation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
